novel_mechanics_found: LEVEL 5 was explored substantially but not won. The four AA99 quadrants are directional controls for a color-8 structure: (44,29)=left, (49,29)=up, (54,29)=right, and (59,29)=down, each in four-pixel increments. Moving 8 up and right until it touches the color-12 slab makes the 8 button at (52,35) latch them; the joined 8/12 assembly can then be routed left, down, and right to form the missing vertical bridge from the start island to the upper island, restored, and followed to the top checker. The large 6 control at (52,49) teleports an avatar standing on either checker. The 2-button material cycle is bidirectional: it closes the row-44 bar from the middle, reaches a fully walled phase, reopens from both ends, and then produces a fully walkable color-12 bridge; an aligned B-shelf also becomes color 12 in that phase. The remaining unexplained obstacle is the color-15/F network: its upper solid socket, lower solid bar, and dotted vertical chute never exchanged solidity under ACTION5, direct clicks, the visible controls, shelf alignment, or tested 2-cycle phases.
narrative: Resolved the required 212-label prefix and replayed it from two fresh resets; both live replays reached frame.levels_completed=4. The first persistent probe exited after that confirmation because its renderer mishandled the frame stack, so its 212 calls were still counted. In the second probe I used rendered grids plus an allowed prior provenance artifact to ground the four directional controls, then live-routed and latched the 8/12 assembly, crossed and restored the temporary bridge, reached the upper checker, and used the 6 control to reach the west stack. I mapped the complete row-44 material cycle from the safe west pad, crossed its all-color-12 phase, and aligned the lower shelf beneath the dotted F chute. Extensive direct investigation of every F object and remaining verb/control produced no traversable chute, so level 5 was not observed won. I stopped at 662 total env.step calls with max_level_reached still 4; no fresh reproduce() gate was run because its 212-action replay would have exceeded the 700-call cap.
gotchas: Direction mapping: ACTION1=up, ACTION2=down, ACTION3=left, ACTION4=right; every move is 2 pixels (sprites are 2x2 on a 2x-upscaled grid).
The rendered frame may be a stack with shape (2,64,64); use the last frame for the current 2D grid.
The AA99 controls move the 8 object rather than rotating it; the fourth quadrant at (59,29) is down and the previously missed quadrant at (54,29) is right.
The 8 button only visibly latches after the 8 object is aligned against the color-12 slab; after latching, direction controls drag both as one assembly.

To bridge the initial vertical gap: latch at the upper-right alignment, move the assembly left to its limit, down three times, then right until the color-12 slab spans rows 22-33; walk left onto the slab before climbing because its right edge is not walkable from the fixed pad.
Restore the assembly before climbing to the top checker: left to the limit, up three, then right three.
The 2-button cycle is reversible and has a distinct all-color-12 full-bridge phase after the fully walled phase; map it while on the fixed west pad and cross only at the full phase.
Further 2-button clicks after crossing close the bridge from the middle and can trap the avatar on the east endpoint because the final support-deleting closure is refused.
Place the B shelf at columns 24-29 before testing the F chute; one more B click wraps it to the left.
The color-15/F chute remained the unresolved frontier; its 2x2 dither always contains void cells and no tested control made it solid.
Blocked moves and refused support-deleting toggles consume env.step budget and advance the visible row-63 tick counter.
